v2.2.12.summary: Stabilizes the vertical hardware HUD so live telemetry and weather updates no longer compress cards and push text outside their borders.
highlights: Uses a fixed 340 × 1200 logical-pixel design size for the vertical HUD, clamped to the display work area; manual resizing is disabled in vertical mode.
Ignores legacy per-display manual heights and applies the same sizing policy on startup and orientation changes, while horizontal HUD resizing remains available.

Prevents the hardware, mini-player, weather and clock sections from flex-shrinking. On shorter work areas, the complete optional three-day forecast is hidden and the remaining HUD content stays scrollable.
v2.2.12.validation: Windows CI Run #258 passed: synchronized version checks, 271/271 main-process regression tests, Renderer TypeScript/Vite build, native WASAPI build, PawnIO resource verification, .NET HardwareService, hardware/storage tests, and Windows installer plus SHA-256 generation.
v2.2.12.caveat: Please visually verify the HUD after all hardware and weather fields load on the target PC, especially on 1080p or shorter work areas; hosted CI cannot verify every physical display layout.

v2.2.11.summary: Adds an extensible China public-holiday calendar based on official State Council notices, with future-year lookup and safe local caching.
highlights: Bundles annual holiday and adjusted-workday schedules for 2017–2027 and parses official notices covering date ranges, abbreviated dates, cross-year dates and make-up workdays.
Looks up unbundled years in the background, validates candidate dates and official government sources, caches accepted results by year and refreshes the calendar through IPC.
Keeps existing cached data when a query or parse fails; it does not guess holidays or workdays for unpublished schedules.
v2.2.11.validation: Windows CI Run #254 passed, including 270/270 main-process regression tests, Renderer TypeScript/Vite, WASAPI, PawnIO, .NET HardwareService, hardware/storage tests, installer packaging and SHA-256 publication.
v2.2.11.caveat: The shipped 2020 schedule still follows the original annual notice and does not include the later January 26, 2020 holiday-extension amendment. Review the versioned build report before relying on historical 2020 dates; future-year networking also needs target-PC verification.

v2.2.10.summary: Separates USB video audio controls from the shared music player and makes simultaneous video and music playback explicit.
highlights: Adds video-specific output-device selection, volume and mute settings, with defaults and migration for older settings.

Allows video audio and Music Service playback to run concurrently. A non-blocking, dismissible overlap notice offers user-selected pause-music or mute-video actions without changing either source when ignored.

Binds a requested non-default audio endpoint before playback; if the endpoint cannot be verified, the video path stays muted and reports the problem instead of silently switching to the Windows default device.
v2.2.10.validation: Windows CI Run #217 passed the version gate, main-process regression tests, Renderer build, native WASAPI, PawnIO, .NET HardwareService, hardware/storage tests, installer packaging and checksum publication.
v2.2.10.caveat: Real video codecs, endpoint hot-plug behavior and sound from the physical USB display speaker still require testing on the target Windows PC. This release does not claim bit-perfect video or music output.

v2.2.9.summary: Unifies playback-mode state across the main player, floating HUD and supported USB display controls.
highlights: Replaces separate shuffle and repeat controls with four modes: Shuffle, Sequential, Repeat One and Repeat All.
Uses a shuffle bag so tracks are not repeated within a shuffle round, then reshuffles for the next round; Previous follows shuffle history.
Persists playback mode and shuffle history in the main-process Music Service and migrates older shuffle/repeat settings.
v2.2.9.validation: Windows CI Run #213 passed the version gate, Node regression suite, Renderer build, native WASAPI, PawnIO, .NET HardwareService, hardware/storage tests, installer packaging, SHA-256 and Release publication.
v2.2.9.caveat: Hosted CI does not play the user's local library. Verify repeat boundaries, shuffle history, pause/resume and actual output devices on the target PC.

v2.2.8.summary: Fixes stale-media and playback-state races encountered during seeking, track changes and repeat playback.
highlights: Invalidates obsolete track/source generations and unloads old media sources when switching tracks, so stale callbacks cannot take control of the active track.
Waits for the seeked event before restoring playback and protects repeat seek/resume from transient paused states.
Adds regression coverage for interrupted play requests and source-generation handling.
v2.2.8.validation: Windows CI Run #209 passed the final code path: version consistency, main-process/music tests, Renderer TypeScript/Vite, native WASAPI, PawnIO, .NET HardwareService, storage tests, installer, checksum and Release publication.
v2.2.8.caveat: Test real local files and seek/repeat boundaries on the target PC; successful automated tests do not prove every codec/profile behaves identically in the user's library.

v2.2.7.summary: Prevents a transient paused state from interrupting the new play request at the end of a looping track.
highlights: Routes media playback through a shared safe-play helper and uses playback-attempt IDs to invalidate stale play promises.
Avoids sending temporary paused state to the main process while an ended-event restart or play request is pending.
Treats expected AbortError interruptions from normal state changes as non-fatal while preserving genuine playback errors.
v2.2.7.validation: Windows CI Run #204 passed the version gate, main-process regression suite, Renderer TypeScript/Vite build, native WASAPI, PawnIO, .NET HardwareService, hardware/storage tests, installer and SHA-256 publication.
v2.2.7.caveat: This fixes the software playback race, not the separate historical P4 WASAPI Exclusive no-sound issue. Verify single-track and playlist loops with the real library.

v2.2.6.summary: Expands weather-source support and makes air-quality categories explicit about the standard used.
highlights: Adds QWeather V1, WeatherCN's standard API and Caiyun V2.6 while retaining Open-Meteo, WeatherAPI and OpenWeather.
Encrypts locally held provider secrets; QWeather uses a locally generated Ed25519 key and JWT, WeatherCN uses its API-key header and cached Location Key, and Caiyun uses HMAC-SHA256 signing.
Carries AQI standard and source metadata through the overview, HUD, USB weather card and Turing weather clock, distinguishing China-MEP from US-EPA values.
v2.2.6.validation: Windows CI Run #201 passed version validation, main and Renderer tests/builds, native WASAPI, PawnIO, .NET HardwareService, hardware/storage tests, installer and Release asset publication.
v2.2.6.caveat: Using a provider requires valid user-owned credentials and service access. Hosted CI does not prove the user's keys, quotas or network path work; test provider connectivity on the target PC.

v2.2.5.summary: Improves global text readability and expands the preferred vertical HUD layout to better fit its monitoring and music content.
highlights: Raises shared typography tokens and improves text sizes in the music library, track lists, player popovers and output-device settings.
Sets the vertical HUD preferred height to 1200 logical pixels while clamping actual bounds to the display work area.
Uses tighter spacing and hides lower-priority multi-day forecast content on short work areas, preserving live metrics, current weather and the clock.
v2.2.5.validation: The published Windows release workflow generated the installer and SHA-256 sidecar. The versioned build report records the initial docking-coordinate assertion mismatch and its correction; do not mistake the first failed run for the final release result.
v2.2.5.caveat: The preferred height is not guaranteed to fit every display or DPI configuration. Verify the full loaded HUD and typography on the target PC.

v2.2.4.summary: Fixes music output-device routing so the shared audio graph is bound to the selected endpoint before playback begins.
highlights: Creates the AudioContext with the selected output-device ID and explicitly sets and verifies its sink before connecting the media element.
Rejects an unavailable non-default endpoint instead of silently connecting to the Windows default output.
Adds regression coverage for sink binding order and failure handling; the normal-output recovery path remains available when the exclusive route fails.
v2.2.4.validation: Windows CI Run #192 passed: 238/238 Node regression tests, Renderer build, native WASAPI, PawnIO, .NET HardwareService, hardware/storage tests, NSIS installer, SHA-256 and Release upload.
v2.2.4.caveat: The Renderer Float32-to-WASAPI path is not claimed to be bit-perfect. Actual P4 endpoint selection, audible output, device changes and recovery must be checked on the target PC.

v2.2.3.summary: Hardens WASAPI playback recovery and adds optional automatic local or online lyrics.
highlights: Does not treat an opened WASAPI endpoint as proof that PCM is rendering; shared output stays audible until native PCM is accepted and rendered.
Falls back to ordinary output if no valid PCM frames arrive within the timeout, and restores the normal audio path after exclusive close or runtime failure.
Prefers a same-name local LRC file, then queries LRCLIB using track metadata only; synchronized lyrics follow playback time while plain lyrics remain readable static text.
v2.2.3.validation: Windows CI Run #186 passed: 238/238 Node regression tests, Renderer build, native WASAPI, PawnIO, .NET HardwareService, storage tests, installer, checksum and Release publication.
v2.2.3.caveat: The lyrics service may be unavailable or rate-limited, and real P4 speaker playback still requires target-PC testing. This release does not claim bit-perfect output.

v2.2.2.summary: Improves WASAPI PCM-format compatibility, especially for mono endpoints, and clarifies USB music-only mode controls.
highlights: Probes both mono and stereo PCM using classic WAVEFORMATEX and WAVEFORMATEXTENSIBLE structures, preferring stereo when a compatible candidate exists.
Adds detailed format-candidate and HRESULT diagnostics, and retries classic WAVEFORMATEX when exclusive initialization rejects the extensible structure.
Keeps the Renderer transport stereo and explicitly downmixes to mono when needed; shortens the music-only action label to “Apply Mode.”
v2.2.2.validation: Windows CI Run #179 passed: 234/234 main-process tests, Renderer build, native WASAPI, PawnIO verification, .NET HardwareService, hardware/storage tests, NSIS installer, SHA-256 and Release publication.
v2.2.2.caveat: Mono downmix changes channel data and is not bit-perfect. The target PC must still verify real P4 speaker output, endpoint isolation and device hot-plug behaviour.

v2.2.1.summary: Introduces the unified local Music Service and the first complete shared-player platform across the app and secondary displays.
highlights: Adds a persistent single playback host, library navigation, playlists, metadata/artwork, M3U/M3U8, ReplayGain, a ten-band equalizer with presets, local LRC lyrics and a sleep timer.
Adds Windows output-device routing and a native WASAPI Exclusive PCM path, plus six USB display modes and a wallpaper-with-background-music mode.
Keeps music playback alive when the main window is hidden to the system tray and preserves the selected USB display identity when restoring output.
v2.2.1.validation: Windows CI Run #175 passed: 225/225 Node tests, Renderer build, native WASAPI, PawnIO verification, .NET HardwareService, storage tests, NSIS installer, SHA-256 and Release upload.
v2.2.1.caveat: Gapless/crossfade dual decks and decoder-to-device bit-perfect playback are not included. Real USB speaker routing, codec playback and sleep/wake behaviour require target-PC acceptance.

v2.2.0.summary: Adds the original global MP3 player and window-lifecycle foundation for music that remains active while the main window is hidden.
highlights: Adds MP3 import and folder scanning, search, playlists, playback controls, seek and application volume, with shuffle and repeat options.
Introduces a single persistent music host shared by the main-window dock, vertical HUD mini-player and supported USB output controls.
Restores the saved USB output display early in startup and keeps audio state in the main process; startup restores track state paused rather than playing unexpectedly.
v2.2.0.validation: The published Windows release includes an NSIS installer and SHA-256 sidecar. The original PR validation passed 188/188 Node tests, but that PR run is not substituted for the final main-branch release build record.
v2.2.0.caveat: This initial release focused on MP3 and the first shared-player foundation; later releases expanded formats, playback controls and output handling. Verify USB display and real audio behaviour on the target PC.

v2.1.8.summary: Fixes the Electron 45 console-message event signature and preserves the existing startup and HUD recovery protections.
highlights: Uses Electron 45's positional console-message callback parameters, correcting the TypeScript errors introduced by treating the second argument as a details object.
Adds a regression test to lock down the event signature and retains first-frame gating, Renderer error handling, legacy-settings tolerance and default HUD startup.
Preserves the earlier USB secondary-display positioning fixes for negative desktop coordinates.
v2.1.8.validation: Windows Server 2025 / Node 24 / .NET 10 CI run 42239092025 passed the 14 version-consistency checks, main tests, Renderer build, PawnIO verification, .NET HardwareService, storage tests, NSIS packaging and SHA-256 generation.
v2.1.8.caveat: COM3 Turing refresh, ESP32-P4 USB display handling, mixed-DPI layouts, hot-plug and long-duration hardware behaviour still require testing on the target Windows PC.

v2.2.13.summary: Returns control of the vertical HUD size to the user, with automatic per-display size memory and a persistent right-click resize lock.
highlights: Restores the saved vertical HUD width and height on startup, prefers a dedicated per-display size record, and migrates compatible portrait dimensions from the older position record.
Adds a checked “Allow Resize” right-click option. Unchecking it disables native resizing and preserves both the selected size and the lock state across application restarts.
Uses 340×900 logical pixels as the first-run default instead of the previous 340×1200 design size; clamps restored bounds to the target display work area and supports resizing down to 280×420.
Keeps horizontal HUD sizing separate and stores portrait dimensions per display so orientation changes do not overwrite the user's vertical size.
v2.2.13.validation: The Windows release workflow for v2.2.13 runs the version gate, main-process regression suite, Renderer TypeScript/Vite build, native WASAPI build, PawnIO resource verification, .NET HardwareService build, storage tests, NSIS packaging and SHA-256 generation. The exact completed run, test count and installer digest will be recorded in the versioned build report after this workflow finishes.
v2.2.13.caveat: Automated tests cannot prove the resized widget's visual comfort on every DPI or monitor configuration. On the target PC, verify native resize handles, content scrolling at shorter heights, saved-size restoration, the checked/unchecked right-click state, orientation switching and display-work-area clamping.
